penalties: Bedford no longer accepts paper test reports directly to the City for this workflow; accepted submission depends on the tester entering the report into Envirotrax and maintaining approved registration.
sourceExcerpt: Bedford requires installation, replacement, repair, relocation, and commercial annual testing, then routes reports and tester approval through VEPO's Envirotrax system.
verdictSummary: Bedford is a strong DFW VEPO page because it combines event-triggered testing, commercial annual testing, online Envirotrax submission, and credential-verified tester approval.
whoIsAffected: Bedford commercial facilities, irrigation systems, and any property with a backflow assembly installed, replaced, repaired, or relocated.
residentialNotes: Residential users are most likely to enter through irrigation installation, replacement, repair, or relocation.

commercialNotes: Commercial facilities must have all backflow protection assemblies tested annually.

annualTesting.summary: Bedford annual testing is strongest for commercial facilities; event-based testing still applies when assemblies are installed, replaced, repaired, or relocated.
highlights: All assemblies are tested on installation, replacement, repair, or relocation.
Envirotrax submission replaces direct paper reports.
workflowSteps: Confirm whether the property is a Bedford commercial facility or has an event-triggered assembly.
Use a BPAT registered through VEPO.
Have the tester submit the report in Envirotrax.

irrigation.summary: Bedford says irrigation systems must have a backflow device installed, with commercial irrigation facilities tested annually and other irrigation work tied to the event trigger.
highlights: Irrigation systems are specifically called out.
Installation, replacement, repair, or relocation still triggers testing.
workflowSteps: Confirm whether the irrigation device is commercial or event-triggered.
Make sure the Envirotrax report matches the irrigation assembly.

fireLine.summary: Bedford states fire protection sprinkler assemblies must be tested or repaired by a BPAT who is a full-time employee of a licensed fire protection sprinkler company.
highlights: Fire protection sprinkler systems are treated separately.
State Fire Marshal licensing and employment context matters.
VEPO registration remains part of the Bedford workflow.
workflowSteps: Identify whether the assembly serves a fire protection sprinkler system.
Use a BPAT who satisfies the State Fire Marshal employment requirement.
Keep the report in Envirotrax rather than a paper-only path.
Use Bedford's official page to classify the assembly trigger.

failureHighlights: Direct paper reporting to Bedford is not the accepted path.
